title: The Startup That Sold $50M of 'Miracle' Water—It Was Tap Water
hook: A startup raised millions by bottling tap water and labeling it as a 'quantum energy' elixir, with fake testimonials from paid actors.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into the outrage about wellness scams and the gullibility of investors—a perfect mix of deception and irony.

title: The Monopoly That Owns Every Lightbulb—and Built in Planned Obsolescence
hook: One company secretly designed lightbulbs to burn out after 1,000 hours, then bought every patent that threatened that plan.
why_this_can_go_viral: Classic dark business history that exposes how corporations intentionally shorten product lives—highly relatable and shareable.

title: The Ad That Used Your Smart TV Camera to Sell You Anxiety Meds
hook: A marketing firm remotely activated smart TV cameras to detect when you looked stressed—then played targeted pharmaceutical ads.
why_this_can_go_viral: Fears about smart devices spying on us are already viral; this confirms the worst-case scenario with terrifying specifics.

title: The Factory That Packed Expired Meat in Bleach to 'Freshen' It
hook: A meatpacking plant used industrial bleach to remove the smell of rotting meat, then sold it to school lunch programs.
why_this_can_go_viral: Shocking, gross, and directly affects consumers—outrage-driven content with massive share potential.

title: The Trader Who Faked a Bank's Bankruptcy with a Single Tweet
hook: One tweet from a hacked account made a bank lose $8 billion in market value—and the trader never got caught.
why_this_can_go_viral: Shows how fragile markets are to digital attacks—blends cyber fear with financial chaos.

title: The Startup That Sold 'AI Hiring'—It Was Just a Guy with a Spreadsheet
hook: A tech startup raised $30M for an AI hiring platform—the algorithm was just a man in a basement manually rejecting resumes.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes the 'fake it till you make it' culture in startups—highly ironic and relatable for job seekers.

title: The Spy Who Infiltrated a Rival's Boardroom by Becoming Their Janitor
hook: A corporate spy spent two years as a janitor, listening to board meetings from the ventilation shafts, and stole $200M in trade secrets.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'undercover janitor' trope is instantly captivating—feels like a movie plot that actually happened.

title: The Ad Campaign That Used Your Internet History to Blackmail You
hook: An ad network discovered your most shameful searches—then served you targeted ads that threatened to reveal them unless you bought their product.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into primal fears about privacy and shame—viewers will immediately check their own browser history.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Organic' Avocados—They Were Soaked in Pesticide
hook: A massive avocado supplier secretly soaked fruit in banned pesticides, then sold it as organic to Whole Foods for a decade.
why_this_can_go_viral: Organic food trust is huge; exposing it as a lie sparks massive debate and shares.

title: The Drug Company That Paid Funeral Homes to Push Its Opioids
hook: A pharmaceutical firm paid funeral directors to recommend their painkillers to grieving families, creating thousands of addicts.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extremely dark and shocking—targets the opioid crisis from a completely new angle.

title: The Trader Who Used a Satellite to Count Cars in Competitor Parking Lots
hook: A hedge fund bought a used satellite and counted cars in factory parking lots to predict earnings before anyone else.
why_this_can_go_viral: Reveals the insane lengths traders go to for an edge—fascinating and tech-heavy.

title: The Startup That Faked a User Base of 1 Billion—with Bots from Bangladesh
hook: A social media startup claimed 1 billion users—they paid a single call center in Bangladesh to run 100,000 fake accounts.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes the 'vanity metrics' culture in Silicon Valley—cynical and highly shareable.

title: The Monopoly That Bought Every Milk Brand—Then Sold You Watered-Down Poison
hook: One dairy conglomerate bought every competitor in the region, then diluted milk with toxic filler to increase profits.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone drinks milk—this feels personal and dangerous, sparking immediate outrage.

title: The Spy Who Posed as a Fire Inspector to Photograph Rival Blueprints
hook: A corporate spy bribed a city official for a fake fire inspector badge, then walked into a rival's office and photographed everything.
why_this_can_go_viral: Simple, clever, and dangerous—viewers love stories about audacious heists.

title: The Ad That Used Your Baby's Cries to Sell You Debt Relief
hook: A marketing firm secretly listened to smart baby monitors, detected crying patterns, and targeted exhausted parents with predatory loan ads.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines parental anxiety with tech horror—extremely emotional and morally outrageous.

title: The Factory That Made 'Luxury' Chocolate—It Was Packed with Lead
hook: A premium chocolate brand used cheap lead-laced cocoa powder from a secret supplier, killing dozens of customers over a decade.
why_this_can_go_viral: Chocolate is universal—learning it could be deadly is visceral and shareable.

title: The Industry Cover-Up of a 'Safe' Baby Shampoo That Caused Blindness
hook: A major baby product company knew its shampoo caused corneal damage in infants—but hid the data for six years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Babies are sacred—harming them for profit triggers maximum emotional response and sharing.

title: The Trader Who Faked a Government Takeover to Dump His Stock
hook: A desperate trader planted a fake news story about a government takeover of his sector, causing a panic, then sold his entire position.
why_this_can_go_viral: Shows how easily markets can be manipulated with fake news—relevant in the age of misinformation.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Biodegradable' Packaging—It Was Just Plastic with a Green Label
hook: A startup raised $100M for 'compostable' packaging—it was ordinary plastic with a fake eco-certification sticker printed in China.
why_this_can_go_viral: Environmental fraud is highly topical—exposes the dark side of the 'green' movement.

title: The Corporation That Paid Hackers to Lock Its Own Systems—for Insurance
hook: A company paid hackers to launch a fake ransomware attack on itself, then collected $50 million in insurance payouts.
why_this_can_go_viral: Turns the ransomware narrative on its head—the company is the criminal, not the victim.
